text:
Alex K: Observed a hard p99 regression in the canary yesterday — 890ms vs SLO 500ms during the 1k qps microbatch sweep. Not steady-state, looks like spikes. Suspect kernel-hop + tool-call loops + cold KV hits.
Maya R: saw that too. I pulled a few traces from the perf logger. two patterns: (A) single big generation where kernel selection spends ~120ms picking a fallback kernel after quant update, (B) repeated tool-call sequences that keep reopening KV entries and force microbatch stalls.
Liam T: do we have a quick perf snippet?
Maya R: pasted below — rough flame-ish extract from the trace:
```
request_id=abc123
total=890ms
 - tokenize: 12ms
 - initial_kernel_pick: 4ms
 - generation_loop: 620ms
    - kernel_hop(softmax->int8_fallback): 120ms
    - kv_fetch_miss: 40ms x 3
    - tool_call + wait_for_tool: 300ms (looped 2x)
 - pack/unpack: 30ms
 - postprocess: 20ms
```
Alex K: kernel_hop is weird — we didn't change any kernel dispatch rules in this canary. But we did push a quantized kernel set last week. Could be heuristic mismatch when sequence lengths spike.
Dina S: I instrumented microbatch queue earlier; here's what I see: under 1k qps with target microbatch=16 we get median batch 14, p95 batch 16, but p99 shows many batches of 32 due to KV-cache misses causing per-request deferral and re-enqueue. That multiplies kernel-selection attempts.
Samir P: KV cache misses -> re-enqueue? explain.
Dina S: When a request triggers a tool call we flush context and requeue the continuation to a fresh microbatch slot. If multiple toolcalls or slow external tool, the continuation waits and the runtime eventually schedules larger aggregation batches to catch up, which causes different kernel pick and longer kernels (due to longer seq length or different kernel path).
Liam T: so tool-call loops amplify microbatch sizing variability -> kernel choices flip -> p99 blows up. That matches traces.
Alex K: actionable triage: 1) verify kernel selection time distribution (not just execution time), 2) test microbatch cap (force max 16) to prevent re-aggregation to 32, 3) add KV-cache warmup for common prefixes, 4) mitigate tool-call loop fastpath.
Maya R: I have a small profiler patch that logs kernel_pick_latency per-request and kernel_candidate_list. Quick snippet to add: 
```
// runtime/kernel_dispatch.cc
log.info("kernel_pick_latency_ms=%d candidates=%s", ms, candidate_summary);
```
I'll push to canary branch for a short run.
Samir P: I'll try reducing microbatch_target from 16 -> 8 on a parallel canary to see p95/p99 delta. If p99 falls a lot, that points to batching-induced kernel mismatches.
Dina S: I'll add an experiment to warm KV for top-500 prefixes during the start of the sweep and measure KV hit rate. If hits go >95% p99 should drop.
Liam T: small mitigation we can roll quickly: if kernel_pick_latency > 50ms, avoid full candidate eval and pick last-known-good kernel for this model+seq_len range. That reduces the 120ms hop cost but might slightly change perf for rare cases. Thoughts?
Alex K: agree as short-term. We need to preserve correctness but prefer consistent latency over best-case raw throughput. Make it opt-in behind feature flag.
Maya R: noted. Also saw one outlier trace where a single request did 5 tool-calls because the user prompt concatenated a chain of external lookups. That single request alone pushed the worker into a longer context path and kernel_pick had to evaluate longer-seq kernels.
Samir P: TLDR experiment plan: (a) microbatch target 8 canary, (b) KV warmup pilot, (c) kernel_pick_latency logging, (d) short-circuit default kernel if pick >50ms behind feature flag.
Dina S: owners: Samir -> a, Dina -> b, Maya -> c, Liam -> d (implement short-circuit). I'll own collecting results and dashboarding p50/p95/p99 by request-class.
Alex K: timeline: get quick runs today (1h each), collate tom. If improvements look good, roll the kernel short-circuit and microbatch change to production-staging for an A/B.
infra-bot: deploy/canary completed: canary-id=canary-2026-11-04-17, config: microbatch_target=16, quant_kernels=v2.
Samir P: starting canary with microbatch_target=8 now — will post results.
Maya R: pushed kernel_pick_latency logging to canary branch and enabled verbose for 30m window.
Alex K: thanks. If anyone hits a clear repro request (long prompt with repeated tool calls), drop me the request_id and I'll run an isolated replay with different kernel configs.
Liam T: small note: also look at memory pinning behavior on fallback kernel paths. We had stray memcpy costs when switching to int8_fallback last year. Could be adding ~20-30ms.
Dina S: good catch. Added memory-copy metric to the instrumentation list.
Alex K: excellent. We'll reconvene after the 1h runs. :thumbsup:
